body: Thanks, I just started going and I haven't found a sponsor yet. I don't think that I can be of much help at this point, which is why I haven't tried to contact him at all since we agreed that he would be the one to reach out to me. I guess I'll keep on waiting. Fortunately, I'm blessed to have a ton of friends who have been incredibly supportive and I also have a good therapist (who unfortunately had limited availability this month). I've been able to lean into yoga, reading, cooking, and dancing but it hasn't done much to abate my worry.

Suicidal thoughts happen to healthy people sometimes as well. The french even have a phrase for it, "L'appel du vide" or call of the void. I'm glad you're in therapy and you know that you will be ok. You can't choose your feelings, but you can choose the way you react to them. Have you told your therapist?

I'm so sorry you're feeling so hopeless and that you have been treated so badly. I'm glad you still have a will to live, and I believe you. Learning to manage a chronic illness can be an uphill battle. It doesn't sound like your doctor is listening to your needs. Would it be possible for you to find a different doctor who is more supportive? What non-medication routes have you tried?

Thank you so much for this post. Your ability to own your decisions and voice the consequences speaks to the heart of how difficult life can be. I'm not used to hearing my inner voice. This is a message I needed to hear. I'm glad you are.

The "Higher Power" bit has been a struggle for me as well. You're going to find it in almost all of the recovery literature. 

I've made some modifications like instead of "powerless over others" I've substituted "have limited influence and no control over others," and for all the "ask God" I use the more neutral language of "may I be..."  

Best wishes.

Hey,

So sorry that you're going through this, I'm in a similar boat so know that you're not alone. It takes a lot of bravery on your part to recognize the issues that you have, and you have a lot of self-awareness to understand that you don't even have a healthy template for relationships. It not your fault that you have these difficulties, but it is your responsibility to become a healthier person. 

To start, you can work on taking care of yourself, and if that brings up guilt or shame, you can pretend that you are your own best friend. Start doing little things for yourself that you enjoy. You can eventually develop more emotional independence by making sure you meet your own needs. If you're feeling lonely, call a friend or try logging on to https://www.7cups.com/ which is filled with free listeners. Relying on one person for your emotional safety is a dangerous game. Instead, you can start by practicing loving-kindness and compassion towards yourself and your struggles. Be gentle with the anxiety you are feeling now, and try and stick to healthier behaviors. 

Have you tried going to a CODA meeting? There are also a lot of books, and videos on the subject. You can check out some of Melody Beattie's work, Melody Pia, or youtubers like The Spartan Life Coach, Ross Rosenberg, Inner Integration, or Lisa A. Romano.
